title: Rebuild the ontology with every term sense and a cross-check test
summary: Retry of rejected job 20261017-173508-0wtc: add docs/ontology.toml (seven seeded terms), a Rust test, and a decision entry. This time Hermes covers both senses, Hermes Agent and the Olympus Orchestration god. Each term carries per-term sources, and a test cross-checks the governing docs for every term name. Audience: agents and checks that read the file, and Sri judging it.

defaults_applied.how: A Rust integration test parses the ontology, with in-memory negative cases and the governing-doc cross-check.
Criteria check Hermes naming both senses and the test failing when a term hit is uncovered.
No email address or personal data in any file.
Definitions are written for an outside reader of Olympus text.
Every term and sense cites a path or decision id that exists.
Four to five files; the earlier extra docs, xtask and architecture deliverables are dropped.
The verifier runs cargo test, clippy and fmt --check.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Start from the base: the earlier attempt's files are gone, so the whole ontology is rebuilt, not patched.
Governing docs for the cross-check are BRIEF.md and docs/decisions.md; the test greps them for each term name.
Each term has senses (each with a source and a part_of_athena yes/no) and excluded_hits (each with a justification); a hit in a governing doc must fall under a cited source or an exclusion.
Under Olympus the system is Olympus; Athena is the strategy and learning role; Hermes is the Orchestration role; Sri is the owner (Zeus). Relations follow that.
Search output for all terms is recorded in the ontology file's excluded-hit justifications and summarized in the decision entry.
The earlier miss: BRIEF.md:597 Pantheon table and BRIEF.md:912 name Hermes as the Orchestration god; line numbers may have shifted, so the producer must re-grep.

acceptance_criteria.text: docs/ontology.toml defines the seven seeded terms (planning, job, Athena, Hermes, product versus system, landed, Sri). Each has a definition, the misread that caused it, a sources field naming existing paths or decision ids, and relations whose targets are all defined terms.

The Hermes entry names both senses, Hermes Agent (the second studied system, Part 2 S1, not part of Athena) and Hermes as the Orchestration god in the Olympus Pantheon (BRIEF.md). It states which sense is part of Olympus and which is not, with a citation for each. Any 'not part of Athena' claim is backed by a source.
Relations match Olympus: the system is Olympus, Athena is the strategy and learning role inside it, and Sri is the owner (Zeus) of Olympus. No relation says the system is Athena.
Every hit of each term name in BRIEF.md is either covered by a listed sense or source, or listed under excluded_hits with a justification. The search results for all terms are recorded in the file.

The file states that a term is added only when it causes a misread and how a check reads it. Landed means merged on main through a verified pull request. The Sri term says to use the name or 'they', never he or she, and cites job 20261017-173504-91ys.

docs/decisions.md has a new entry keeping the ontology, citing the Olympus 2026-10-17 decision sheet (decision 5). It lists alternatives (no ontology; per-study glossaries only), says studies keep their own concept model so firstmate, Hermes Agent and Athena are compared in the same terms, and describes the cross-check. docs/decision-links.toml is updated if the repo requires it. CHANGELOG.md has an entry.

Run `cargo test`: the new ontology test passes on docs/ontology.toml. Unit tests on in-memory input show it failing on a missing sources field, a non-existent source, a dangling relation target, a duplicate term, and a term name that appears in a governing doc but is covered by neither a sense nor an exclusion. `cargo clippy` is clean and `cargo fmt --check` passes.
No secrets or personal data, including the user's email address, appear in any new or changed file.

out_of_scope: Changing BRIEF.md or other governing documents
docs/ontology.md, xtask tests and architecture.md changes
Adding terms beyond the seven seeded misreads
Changes to athena.toml, defaults.toml or workflows
departures: Slightly higher cost and lower pass probability than the reference: the cross-check test needs grep-style matching on BRIEF.md, and the previous attempt failed on content accuracy.
